answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit bids, then slash that stake when a challenge proves coordinated fraud. A vine of linked accounts may look diverse, but shared funding and repeated behavior can trigger a delayed audit; pigment marks the risk score, while zephyr names the cooling-off period before funds unlock. Creating more identities therefore multiplies capital at risk and ties it up, making a Sybil attack costly rather than merely a matter of minting accounts.
